## Table 1 (appendix; tables/table1_audit.tex), generated by figures/scripts/table1_audit.py from experiment-repo results/audit.csv
Title: Data audit of the 13 binary score matrices after de-duplication.
Note: Rows are the file names of the data repository (commit 55faff49). Models: rows kept after dropping repeated model names and rows identical to an earlier row ("Dup. dropped" counts both). Families: distinct model families derived from the names by keyword (heuristic); for LegalBench the row-to-model mapping is not published, so families are unknown and every row counts as its own. Constant items: items answered identically by all models (kept). Full score: min / median / max of the models' full-benchmark accuracy. All matrices were checked to be binary.

## Fig. 1 (main text; figures/fig1_protocol.pdf), figures/scripts/fig1_protocol.py (no data)
Caption: The protocol. A design picks n items using only the source models' results; the target model is run on those n items only; an estimator turns its n answers (and the source matrix) into a predicted full-benchmark score, which is compared with the true score. The three splits differ in which models play the target.

## Table 2 (main text; tables/table2_primary.tex), figures/scripts/tables234.py from results/primary.csv and results/selected.csv
Title: Primary endpoint: RMSE of the predicted full score relative to uniform random sampling, n = 100 items.
Note: Entry = geometric mean over benchmarks of RMSE / RMSE of uniform × mean on the same targets and draws, [95% family-bootstrap interval; 2000 replicates, target families resampled within each benchmark]. Below 1 is better than uniform. Thin cells (< 10 targets or < 5 families) are excluded; the lineage split is defined for 12 benchmarks (LegalBench has no family information). Methods are design × estimator; the first seven rows are fixed class representatives (one per method class), the last three are the best methods by this endpoint and were chosen after seeing the results, so their intervals and ratios are optimistic. Third block: for each of five method classes, the cell chosen by leave-one-benchmark-out (the cell with the smallest geometric-mean ratio on the other benchmarks of the same split is applied to the held-out benchmark; the row is the geometric mean over held-out benchmarks), which does not use the outcomes of the benchmark it is scored on. Last block: same quantity against stratified × mean as the baseline. The bottom rows count benchmarks, targets and target families, summed over the benchmarks entering. Benchmarks are not independent (HELM models recur across its benchmarks, OLL families across OLL benchmarks); the interval reflects target-family sampling only.

shown.message:
I made Figs. 1, 2, 3 and 5 shorter, pushed them to `figtab-repo` `main` (7fa22cb), and closed #4 with a comment to `paper-repo`. I haven't compiled them into the paper, so I haven't checked how much page space they save.

| Figure | Before | Now | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fig. 1 | 181 pt | 115 pt | Pipeline boxes in one row, splits listed below, true-score box under the estimator. |
| Fig. 2 | 269 pt | 166 pt | One row of three panels with a shared y axis, legend below in 4 columns. I thinned the x ticks to 10, 50, 100 and 400. |
| Fig. 3 | 246 pt | 191 pt | Same two panels, bands and legend, but the legend now runs in 4 columns. |
| Fig. 5 | 231 pt | 187 pt | Legend moved to the right of the panels. The thin benchmarks are one hollow grey entry, as the caption already says. |

- **Content:** Method classes, bands, benchmark counts and the notes are unchanged, so no claim is lost and the captions stay as they were.
- **Type size:** Text is at least 7 pt, and Fig. 1 is at 7.5 pt.
- **Width:** Each is saved at exactly 396 pt wide, so `width=\textwidth` no longer rescales them.
- **Other figures:** I switched the shared math font to STIX so it matches the serif text, which regenerated Figs. 4, 5b and 6 as well. Their sizes are unchanged. I also stopped tracking `__pycache__` in the repo.

I viewed Figs. 1, 2 and 5 at reduced resolution. I only read the size of Fig. 3 and did not look at it after the last tweak. I also added the new heights to `figures/README.md`.
